svg.title: Where parallelism comes from
svg.desc: Four small ADGs: a single chain, a fork and join, two independent chains, and a graph whose extra edge only looks like a fork. Each has its earliest-start Gantt chart, work, span and width.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: 1 One chain: nothing runs in parallel

g.text: Durations invented. Gantt charts are earliest-start schedules (every action starts as soon as its predecessors finish). Width = largest set of pairwise unordered actions, computed by brute force.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Two actions can run at the same time only if neither reaches the other. A graph whose transitive reduction is one chain is a strict sequence, however many robots it involves.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
